in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, do you have a child or children that you're responsible for?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do. I have one child, Alex, who's 8 years old and lives with me at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. It's helpful to know you have Alex who is 8 years old and lives with you.

To continue assessing your eligibility, I need to ask: Are you and Alex currently living in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, we both live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Now I need to ask about your responsibility for Alex.

Are you the person responsible for Alex? This typically means you're the parent or the main person who looks after Alex on a day-to-day basis (for example, you provide their care, make decisions about their upbringing, and they live with you).

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, yes, I'm their parent and they live with me, but I should mention that Alex has been in local authority care for a few months now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know that important detail. I need to understand this situation a bit better.

When you say Alex has been in local authority care for a few months, does Alex still live with you at home, or are they living elsewhere (for example, with foster carers or in a care home)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: They're living elsewhere - they're not at home with me while they're in care.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. This is an important detail for determining eligibility.

Can I ask: Are you still receiving Child Benefit payments for Alex currently, or have the payments stopped since Alex went into local authority care?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not currently receiving Child Benefit - that's why I'm asking whether I'm eligible to claim it.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that.

I need to understand one more thing about Alex's care situation: Is the local authority paying for Alex's accommodation (where they're living now), or are you paying for it?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: The local authority is paying for it - they're covering the costs of Alex's accommodation.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm sorry to inform you that **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex** at this time.

Here's why: While Alex is 8 years old (which would normally qualify based on age), the key issue is that Alex is currently being looked after by the local authority and is living away from your home. Since the local authority is paying for Alex's accommodation, you cannot receive Child Benefit during this period. This is because the local authority has taken on the responsibility for Alex's care and maintenance while they are in care.

**Important to note:** If Alex's care situation changes in the future - for example, if Alex returns to live with you at home - you would be able to claim Child Benefit again at that point. You should contact the Child Benefit Office when circumstances change to make a new claim.

I understand this may be disappointing news, but please feel free to ask if you have any questions about this decision.
